what_its_for: This eye drop is used to lower high pressure inside your eye. It is prescribed for adults with a condition called open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension (high eye pressure). Lowering eye pressure helps protect your vision and prevents damage to the optic nerve.
how_to_take: Wash your hands thoroughly before using this medicine. Tilt your head back, gently pull down your lower eyelid to create a small pocket, and place one drop into that pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes — do not blink or squeeze your eye shut hard. Press gently on the inner corner of your eye (near the nose) with your finger for about 1 to 2 minutes to keep the medicine from draining away. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before putting in the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting your contacts back in. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 minutes between each different eye drop.
dosing: Use ONE drop in the affected eye or eyes ONCE daily in the EVENING. Do not use more than one drop per eye per day. Using it more than once a day may actually make it work less well.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and use your next drop the following evening at your regular time. Do not double up or use two doses in one day to make up for the missed one.
storage: Store the unopened bottle in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Once you open the bottle, you may store it in the refrigerator OR at room temperature up to 77°F (25°C). Keep it away from direct sunlight and heat. Throw away any unused medicine 6 weeks after opening the bottle, even if there is still liquid left. Keep this medicine out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not touch the tip of the dropper bottle to your eye, fingers, or any surface — this can contaminate the drops and cause an eye infection. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery right after using the drops until your vision clears. Do not use this medicine while wearing contact lenses — remove lenses first and wait 15 minutes before reinserting them.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: sudden vision changes or vision loss, severe eye pain or increased eye redness, signs of eye infection (discharge, swelling, or crusting), swelling of the eyelids or face, difficulty breathing, chest pain, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash or hives. Also let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Tell your doctor if you notice your eye color gradually changing (iris may become more brown over time) or if your eyelashes appear darker, longer, or thicker — these are known side effects of latanoprost.
when_it_works: This medication begins lowering eye pressure within a few hours of the first dose, but it may take several weeks of regular use to see the full effect. It is very important to keep using it every day even if your eyes feel fine, because high eye pressure often has no symptoms. Your doctor will check your eye pressure at follow-up visits to make sure the medicine is working well.
special_populations: This medicine has not been studied in children and is approved for use in adults only. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this eye drop, as it may be absorbed into your bloodstream in small amounts. Use with caution if you have had eye surgery, active eye inflammation (uveitis), or if you only have one functioning eye — your doctor will guide you. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting this medication.
